topic.name: The Average of the Roots Formula

question.text: Find the axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(7-5x)(x+1).$
question.explanation:
From the equation $y=(7-5x)(x+1),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=\dfrac75$ and $x_2=-1.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac75-1\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac75-\dfrac55\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{2}{5} \right)}{2}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{1}{5} \end{align*}

Therefore, the axis of symmetry is $x=\dfrac{1}{5}.$

example.title: Finding the Axis of Symmetry From the Parabola’s Equation in Factored Form

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(2x+k)(x-3k)$ is $x=\dfrac 14.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we will calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\dfrac 14,$ we will set our result equal to $\dfrac 14.$

From the equation $y=(2x+k)(x-3k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=-\dfrac{k}{2}$ and $x_2=3k.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{k}{2}+3k\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{6k-k}{2}\right)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5k}{4} \end{align*}

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=\dfrac 14.$ Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} \dfrac{5k}{4} &= \dfrac 14 \\[5pt] 5k &= 1 \\[5pt] k &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac 15}. \end{align*}

example.title: Finding an Unknown Value Given the Axis of Symmetry

question.text: The axis of symmetry of the parabola $y=(x-5k)(x+7k)$ is $x=4.$ Find the value of $k.$
question.explanation:
First, we calculate the axis of symmetry in terms of $k.$ Then, since we know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4,$ we will set our result equal to $4.$

From the equation $y=(x-5k)(x+7k),$ we find that the roots of the parabola are $x_1=5k$ and $x_2=-7k.$

To find the axis of symmetry, we take the average of the roots, as follows:

\begin{align*} x &= \dfrac{x_1+x_2}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5k +(-7k)}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{-2k}{2}\\[5pt] &= -k \end{align*}

We know that the axis of symmetry is $x=4.$ Therefore, we have \begin{align} -k & = 4\\[5pt] k & = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-4}. \end{align}
